samples.query: How should I structure my answer when asked about optimizing database query performance?

retrieved_context.content: Project: Analytics Pipeline Overhaul. Identified slow PostgreSQL reporting queries causing 4-second API latencies. Implemented compound B-tree indexing and a Redis caching layer, decreasing response time by 65% to 1.4 seconds.
STAR Framework: Situation (context/problem), Task (your goal/responsibility), Action (specific technical actions taken), Result (quantified business impact).

samples.reference_answer: Structure your answer using the STAR method: Situation (explain slow 4-second PostgreSQL queries on the analytics pipeline), Task (reduce latency for downstream API users), Action (implemented compound B-tree indexes and Redis caching), and Result (quantify the 65% reduction in latency to 1.4 seconds).
prohibited_hallucinations: migrated all data to Cassandra NoSQL

samples.query: How can I improve my machine learning bullet points to stand out to hiring managers?

retrieved_context.content: Current bullet: 'Fine-tuned BERT model for text classification and improved inference latency with ONNX Runtime, achieving 92% F1 score and 40% latency reduction.'
Effective engineering resume bullets follow the formula: Accomplished [X] as measured by [Y] by doing [Z]. Always lead with strong action verbs and quantify outcomes.

samples.reference_answer: Your bullet point already demonstrates strong impact by pairing technical action with quantified outcomes: achieved a 92% F1 score and a 40% latency reduction using BERT and ONNX Runtime. Keep emphasizing both the performance metric (92% F1) and operational efficiency (40% latency reduction).
prohibited_hallucinations: must publish at least 3 NeurIPS papers
remove all mentions of Python and machine learning
guarantees an immediate VP of AI position
